```{r Load packages and config}

library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
sf_use_s2(FALSE)

source(here::here("analysis", "0-config.R"))
source(here::here("analysis", "0-functions.R"))

# No step below is stochastic (all models are pre-fit; predictions are cached;
# loess/lm are deterministic), but a seed is set for reproducibility per house

set.seed(20260817)

# Overview

The primary model M1 constrains the treatment contrast to a plane in the two
coordinates: the log rate ratio varies as `a0 + a1 * lat_c + a2 * lon_c`. This
script asks two questions, both as **sensitivity analyses** — M1 stays primary
no matter what these show:

1. **Is the plane adequate?** Three progressively more flexible treatment
   surfaces (M2 additive splines, M3 quadratic contrast, M4 arm-specific Matern
   field) are compared to M1 by surface agreement, AIC, a nested LRT (M3 only),
   and the back-transformed SD of the M4 deviation field.
2. **Does baseline heterogeneity explain the ATE heterogeneity?** If the RR
   surface is just a reflection of where baseline mortality is high, control-arm
   log mortality and log RR should track each other. They do not: the baseline
   gradient runs roughly north–south while the RR gradient runs roughly
   east–west (the "oblique ATE surface" of the Discussion).

With 1,084 treated deaths, the expected outcome is that M2–M4 reproduce the
plane. A null here is a **result** — it bounds the magnitude of any missed
curvature ("consistent with the linear specification being adequate at the
resolution these data support"), it is not an absence of evidence.

```{r Load cached fits and prediction surfaces}

# --- Cached model fits (fit in 02A) ----
m1 <- readRDS(here("data", "fitmort_child_gen_krig_int.rds"))    # linear plane (primary)
m2 <- readRDS(here("data", "fitmort_child_gen_krig_spline.rds")) # additive splines df = 4
m3 <- readRDS(here("data", "fitmort_child_gen_krig_poly.rds"))   # quadratic contrast +3 df
m4 <- readRDS(here("data", "fitmort_child_doub_matern.rds"))     # arm-specific Matern field

# Human-readable labels and lettered panels, in the M1..M4 order used throughout.
model_key <- tibble::tribble(
  ~model,             ~mnum, ~panel, ~label,
  "gen_krig_int",     "M1",  "A",    "M1: linear plane (primary)",
  "gen_krig_spline",  "M2",  "B",    "M2: additive splines (df 4)",
  "gen_krig_poly",    "M3",  "C",    "M3: quadratic contrast",
  "doub_matern",      "M4",  "D",    "M4: arm-specific Matern field"
)

# --- Cached prediction surfaces (built in 02A: get_grid_preds_both_tx over ----
# --- boxgrid, then differenced). One row per grid cell per model. ----
ate_preds <- readRDS(here("data", "preds_ATE.rds"))

# District outlines for the maps.
niger_adm2_sub <- readRDS(here("data", "niger_adm2_sub.rds"))

# Restrict to the four models this script compares and derive log RR + log
# baseline. rate_ratio = predTreatment / predControl is already on the surface.
preds4 <- ate_preds %>%
  dplyr::filter(model %in% model_key$model) %>%
  mutate(
    log_rr        = log(rate_ratio),
    log_base_ctrl = log(predControl)   # control-arm log mortality rate
  ) %>%
  left_join(model_key, by = "model")

# The four surfaces are predicted on the same boxgrid in the same row order
# (verified: coordinates are identical across models), so cross-model
# quantities can be aligned by within-model row index rather than a spatial join.
n_cells <- preds4 %>% st_drop_geometry() %>% count(model) %>% pull(n) %>% unique()
stopifnot(length(n_cells) == 1L)
```

# Shared map scaffolding ----

```{r base map}

# Reused from 06C: white land, district outlines, scale bar, north arrow.
base_map <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = niger_adm2_sub, fill = "white", color = "black", size = 0.25) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  annotation_scale(height = unit(0.15, "cm")) +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Longitude") +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Latitude") +
  theme(
    legend.position   = "bottom",
    legend.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    legend.title       = element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5),
    strip.text         = element_text(hjust = 0, face = "bold")
  )

# rasterise_surface(): pull one model's grid column, rasterise to WGS84.
# Local helper (used 4x below); kept here rather than in 0-functions.R because
# it is specific to this script's preds4 object.
rasterise_surface <- function(preds_sf, model_name, colname) {
  one <- preds_sf %>%
    dplyr::filter(model == model_name) %>%
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(colname))
  rast <- make_raster_map(one, proj_crs, global_crs, colname)
  as.data.frame(rast, xy = TRUE, na.rm = FALSE) %>%
    dplyr::rename(value = dplyr::all_of(colname))
}
```

# 4. Is the plane adequate?

## 4.1 RR surface grid (Supplementary Figure 4, multi-panel) ----

Panel A is the current Supplementary Figure 4 (the primary-model RR surface);
panels B–D add the flexible models. **All four panels share one colour scale,
one set of limits (0.5–1.5), and identical clipping** (values are squished to
the limits, but in fact no cell falls outside them), a diverging palette centred
at RR = 1. Read across the row: if the flexible surfaces reproduce panel A, the
plane is capturing the spatial RR structure these data support.

```{r Supp Fig 4 multi-panel RR surfaces}

rr_raster_df <- purrr::map_dfr(
  model_key$model,
  ~ rasterise_surface(preds4, .x, "rate_ratio") %>% mutate(model = .x)
) %>%
  left_join(model_key, by = "model") %>%
  mutate(panel_label = paste0(panel, "  ", label),
         panel_label = factor(panel_label,
                              levels = paste0(model_key$panel, "  ", model_key$label)))

supp_fig4 <- base_map +
  geom_raster(data = rr_raster_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = value), na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_sf(data = niger_adm2_sub, fill = NA, color = "grey20", size = 0.15) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel_label, nrow = 2) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = muted("#009392FF"), mid = "white", high = muted("#D0587EFF"),
    transform = "log", midpoint = 1,
    limits = c(0.5, 1.5), breaks = seq(0.5, 1.5, by = 0.25),
    oob = scales::squish, na.value = NA,
    guide = guide_colorbar(
      title = "Modeled mortality rate ratio (treated / control)",
      title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5,
      label.position = "bottom", label.hjust = 0.5,
      barheight = unit(10, "pt"), barwidth = unit(220, "pt"),
      ticks.colour = "white", ticks.linewidth = 1, frame.colour = "white"))

supp_fig4

ggsave(
  filename = here("results", "manuscript", "supp_fig4-modeled_ATE_rate_ratios.png"),
  plot = supp_fig4, width = 8, height = 8.5, units = "in", dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

> **Note on Supplementary Figure 4.** This chunk now writes the canonical
> multi-panel version of `supp_fig4-modeled_ATE_rate_ratios.png`. The
> single-panel chunk in `06C-supp_mtrl.qmd` produces panel A alone and is
> superseded; render 08 after 06C (or retire the 06C chunk) so the multi-panel
> figure is the one that survives.

## 4.2 Surface correlation matrix ----

Pearson correlation of predicted **log RR** across grid cells, for every pair of
models. High off-diagonal correlations mean the flexible surfaces are re-drawing
the same RR gradient the plane draws.

```{r log RR surface correlation matrix}

# Wide matrix: one column of log RR per model, rows aligned by grid cell.
log_rr_wide <- preds4 %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  mutate(cell = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(cell, mnum, log_rr) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = mnum, values_from = log_rr) %>%
  dplyr::select(-cell)

surface_cor_matrix <- cor(log_rr_wide, method = "pearson")

surface_cor_df <- as.data.frame(round(surface_cor_matrix, 3))

surface_cor_df %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Pearson correlation of predicted log RR across grid cells.")
```

## 4.3 sd(delta) from M4 ----

M4 carries a shared field `w(s)` common to both arms plus a treated-arm
deviation field `delta(s)`; log RR(s) = (planar contrast) + delta(s), so the SD
of `delta` is directly the SD of log RR contributed by the extra field. We
back-transform it to an approximate multiplicative spread in RR and place it
against the trial-wide 14% relative effect for scale.

```{r sd delta from M4}

# spaMM stores each random effect's variance in $lambda. Field 2 is the
# deviation field (0 + isTreated_child_num | lon + lat); its lambda is the
# variance of delta on the log scale.
lambda_delta <- m4$lambda[["lon + lat.1.isTreated_child_num"]]
sd_delta     <- sqrt(lambda_delta)

# Back-transform: multiplicative spread in RR around the planar prediction.
pct_rr_spread <- (exp(sd_delta) - 1) * 100

# The deviation field's own Matern range, to interpret WHAT kind of variation
# sd_delta represents (smooth spatial gradient vs. village-level scatter).
rho_delta   <- m4$CorrEst_and_RanFix$corrPars[["2"]]$rho
nu_delta    <- m4$CorrEst_and_RanFix$corrPars[["2"]]$nu
range_delta_km <- 1 / (1000 * rho_delta)

cat(sprintf("sd(delta) on log scale        : %.3f\n", sd_delta))
cat(sprintf("~ multiplicative RR spread     : +/- %.1f%% (exp(sd) - 1)\n", pct_rr_spread))
cat(sprintf("trial-wide relative effect     : 14%% (RR ~ 0.86) for scale\n"))
cat(sprintf("deviation-field Matern range   : %.2f km (nu = %.1f)\n", range_delta_km, nu_delta))
```

`r sprintf("sd(delta) = %.3f", sd_delta)` on the log scale corresponds to roughly
`r sprintf("+/-%.0f%%", pct_rr_spread)` multiplicative spread in the rate ratio
around the planar prediction. But the deviation field's Matern range is only
`r sprintf("%.2f km", range_delta_km)` — shorter than the spacing between
villages — so this spread is **short-range, village-level scatter, not a smooth
spatial gradient the plane misses**. That is the sense in which the plane is
adequate: what the extra field adds is nugget-like noise, not curvature.

## 4.4 Model comparison table ----

```{r model comparison table}

# matern_field1(): rho / range(km) / nu of the shared spatial field (field 1),
# so all four models are described on the same footing. (For M2 these are not
# comparable to the others because the splined MAIN effects compete with the
# field for the baseline surface — see footnote.)
matern_field1 <- function(fit) {
  cp  <- fit$CorrEst_and_RanFix$corrPars[["1"]]
  tibble(rho = cp$rho, range_km = 1 / (1000 * cp$rho), nu = cp$nu)
}

# Estimated-parameter count k that matches the marginal AIC penalty spaMM
# reports (fixef + lambda + corrPars): the df that goes WITH the AIC column.
param_k <- function(fit) sum(unlist(fit$dfs))

# Nested LRT, M3 vs M1 (3 df): M1 is nested in M3 (linear terms retained).
lrt_m3 <- lrt_manual(m3, m1)

# M4 vs M1 tests a variance component at its boundary (lambda_delta >= 0). The
# fixed effects are identical, so lrt_manual() does not apply; compute the
# deviance directly. Nominal 1 df on the variance; the null distribution is a
# 0.5 chi2_0 + 0.5 chi2_1 mixture, so the naive p is halved and is conservative.
ll_m1 <- as.numeric(logLik(m1, which = "p_v"))
ll_m4 <- as.numeric(logLik(m4, which = "p_v"))
chi2_m4 <- 2 * (ll_m4 - ll_m1)
p_m4_mixture <- 0.5 * pchisq(chi2_m4, df = 1, lower.tail = FALSE)

model_comparison <- bind_rows(
  tibble(mnum = "M1",
         terms = "trt + lat_c + lon_c + trt:lat_c + trt:lon_c",
         matern_field1(m1)),
  tibble(mnum = "M2",
         terms = "ns(lat_c,4)+ns(lon_c,4) + trt + trt:ns(lat_c,4)+trt:ns(lon_c,4)",
         matern_field1(m2)),
  tibble(mnum = "M3",
         terms = "M1 + trt:lat_c^2 + trt:lon_c^2 + trt:lat_c:lon_c",
         matern_field1(m3)),
  tibble(mnum = "M4",
         terms = "M1 + Matern(0 + trt | lat+lon)",
         matern_field1(m4))
) %>%
  left_join(model_key %>% dplyr::select(mnum, label), by = "mnum") %>%
  mutate(
    aic    = c(AIC(m1)[1], AIC(m2)[1], AIC(m3)[1], AIC(m4)[1]),
    params = c(param_k(m1), param_k(m2), param_k(m3), param_k(m4)),
    lrt_vs_m1_chi2 = c(NA, NA, lrt_m3$chi2_LR, chi2_m4),
    lrt_vs_m1_df   = c(NA, NA, lrt_m3$df,      1),
    lrt_vs_m1_p    = c(NA, NA, lrt_m3$p_value, p_m4_mixture),
    sd_delta = c(NA, NA, NA, sd_delta)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(model = label, mnum, terms, aic, params,
                lrt_vs_m1_chi2, lrt_vs_m1_df, lrt_vs_m1_p,
                rho, range_km, nu, sd_delta)

model_comparison %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4))) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    caption = paste(
      "Model comparison. AIC is the marginal AIC; `params` is the matching",
      "parameter count (fixed effects + variance/correlation parameters).",
      "LRT is vs M1. M3 vs M1 is a valid 3-df nested test (M1 is nested in M3:",
      "the linear interaction terms are retained and only the treatment contrast",
      "is made quadratic; coordinate MAIN effects stay linear). M4 vs M1 tests a",
      "variance component at the boundary: df = 1 nominal, null distribution",
      "~ 0.5*chi2_0 + 0.5*chi2_1, so the reported p is halved and is conservative.",
      "M2 is not nested in M1 or M3 (splines replace, not add to, the linear",
      "terms), so its LRT cells are blank and it is compared by AIC only.",
      "rho/range/nu describe the shared Matern field (field 1); for M2 these are",
      "NOT comparable to the others because the splined main effects compete with",
      "the field for the baseline surface. sd(delta) is the M4 deviation-field SD."))
```

## 4.5 Difference surfaces ----

Flexible RR minus M1 RR, for M3 and M4. If departures from the plane were real
signal they would sit in the **interior**; if they are edge effects they cluster
at the **perimeter** where the flexible bases and the extra field are least
constrained.

```{r RR difference surfaces M3 M4 vs M1}

# rate_ratio aligned by grid cell (same order across models), differenced vs M1.
rr_by_cell <- preds4 %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  mutate(cell = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(cell, mnum, rate_ratio) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = mnum, values_from = rate_ratio)

# Attach geometry from the M1 rows (canonical cell order) and build diffs.
m1_geom <- preds4 %>% dplyr::filter(mnum == "M1") %>%
  mutate(cell = row_number()) %>% dplyr::select(cell, geometry)

diff_sf <- m1_geom %>%
  left_join(rr_by_cell, by = "cell") %>%
  mutate(`M3 - M1` = M3 - M1, `M4 - M1` = M4 - M1)

diff_raster_df <- purrr::map_dfr(
  c("M3 - M1", "M4 - M1"),
  function(cn) {
    one <- diff_sf %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(cn))
    rast <- make_raster_map(one, proj_crs, global_crs, cn)
    as.data.frame(rast, xy = TRUE, na.rm = FALSE) %>%
      dplyr::rename(value = dplyr::all_of(cn)) %>%
      mutate(contrast = cn)
  }
)

diff_lim <- max(abs(diff_raster_df$value), na.rm = TRUE)

diff_surfaces <- base_map +
  geom_raster(data = diff_raster_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = value), na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_sf(data = niger_adm2_sub, fill = NA, color = "grey20", size = 0.15) +
  facet_wrap(~ contrast, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = muted("#4B0055"), mid = "white", high = muted("#007D34"),
    midpoint = 0, limits = c(-diff_lim, diff_lim), na.value = NA,
    guide = guide_colorbar(
      title = "RR difference (flexible - M1)",
      title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5,
      barheight = unit(10, "pt"), barwidth = unit(200, "pt")))

diff_surfaces

ggsave(
  filename = here("results", "figs", "linearity-rr-difference-surfaces.png"),
  plot = diff_surfaces, width = 8, height = 4.6, units = "in", dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

# 5. Does baseline heterogeneity explain the ATE heterogeneity?

## 5.1 Baseline log mortality vs log RR ----

One point per grid cell: control-arm log mortality (x) against log RR (y), for
M1 and M4. If baseline heterogeneity explained the ATE heterogeneity the cloud
would be flat (constant RR) — or, if RR simply tracked baseline, it would lie on
a tight line. A shallow slope with wide vertical spread means the RR gradient is
**not** a reflection of the baseline gradient.

```{r baseline vs log RR scatter}

scatter_dat <- preds4 %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::filter(mnum %in% c("M1", "M4")) %>%
  dplyr::select(mnum, label, log_base_ctrl, log_rr)

# Slope and spread per model: OLS slope of log RR on baseline log mortality,
# plus the residual SD (spread of log RR not explained by baseline) and the
# marginal SD of log RR for reference.
baseline_rr_fit <- scatter_dat %>%
  group_by(mnum) %>%
  summarise(
    slope        = coef(lm(log_rr ~ log_base_ctrl))[2],
    r_squared    = summary(lm(log_rr ~ log_base_ctrl))$r.squared,
    resid_sd     = sd(residuals(lm(log_rr ~ log_base_ctrl))),
    logrr_sd     = sd(log_rr),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

baseline_rr_fit %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Log RR regressed on control-arm log mortality, per grid cell.",
    "A near-flat slope and R^2 well below 1 indicate baseline heterogeneity",
    "does not account for the RR heterogeneity."))

baseline_vs_rr <- ggplot(scatter_dat, aes(x = log_base_ctrl, y = log_rr)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.3, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, colour = "#D0587EFF", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = "#009392FF",
              linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.25) +
  facet_wrap(~ label, nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = "Predicted control-arm log mortality rate",
       y = "Predicted log rate ratio (treated / control)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(hjust = 0, face = "bold"))

baseline_vs_rr

ggsave(
  filename = here("results", "figs", "linearity-baseline-vs-logRR-scatter.png"),
  plot = baseline_vs_rr, width = 8, height = 4.2, units = "in", dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

## 5.2 M1 baseline surface and RR surface, side by side ----

The baseline mortality gradient runs roughly north–south; the RR gradient runs

```{r M1 baseline surface and RR surface}

  theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(face = "bold"))

p_rr <- base_map +
  geom_raster(data = rr_rast_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = value), na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_sf(data = niger_adm2_sub, fill = NA, color = "grey20", size = 0.15) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = muted("#009392FF"), mid = "white", high = muted("#D0587EFF"),
    transform = "log", midpoint = 1, limits = c(0.5, 1.5),
    breaks = seq(0.5, 1.5, by = 0.25), oob = scales::squish, na.value = NA,
    guide = guide_colorbar(title = "Rate ratio",
                           barheight = unit(10, "pt"), barwidth = unit(150, "pt"))) +
  labs(subtitle = "B  Rate ratio (treated / control)") +
  theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(face = "bold"))

m1_baseline_vs_rr <- p_base + p_rr

m1_baseline_vs_rr

ggsave(
  filename = here("results", "figs", "linearity-M1-baseline-vs-RR.png"),
  plot = m1_baseline_vs_rr, width = 9, height = 5, units = "in", dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

# 6. Robustness: arm-stratified residual smooths ----

Pearson residuals from M1, smoothed separately over space within treated and
control villages. If the plane were hiding RR structure, the two smoothed
residual surfaces would diverge (systematically positive where one arm is
under-predicted and the other over-predicted). This is an internal diagnostic —
it belongs in the supplement only if it shows something.

```{r arm-stratified residual smooths}

# Fitting data with Pearson residuals, in UTM (projected) coordinates.
resid_dat <- m1$data %>%
  mutate(pearson_resid = residuals(m1, type = "pearson"))

# loess surface of residuals within each arm, predicted back onto the boxgrid
# cells (deterministic; NA outside the data hull, which drops out). span chosen
# for a broad regional smooth, not local wiggle.
grid_xy <- preds4 %>%
  dplyr::filter(mnum == "M1") %>%
  mutate(x = st_coordinates(.)[, 1], y = st_coordinates(.)[, 2]) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::select(x, y)

smooth_one_arm <- function(arm_label) {
  d <- resid_dat %>% dplyr::filter(isTreated_child == arm_label)
  fit <- loess(pearson_resid ~ lon + lat, data = d, span = 0.5, degree = 1,
               control = loess.control(surface = "direct"))
  preds <- predict(fit, newdata = tibble(lon = grid_xy$x, lat = grid_xy$y))
  tibble(x = grid_xy$x, y = grid_xy$y, value = as.numeric(preds),
         arm = arm_label)
}

resid_smooth <- purrr::map_dfr(c("Control", "Treatment"), smooth_one_arm)

# rasterise each arm's smoothed surface for mapping.
resid_smooth_sf <- st_as_sf(resid_smooth %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(value)),
                            coords = c("x", "y"), crs = proj_crs)

resid_raster_df <- purrr::map_dfr(
  c("Control", "Treatment"),
  function(a) {
    one <- resid_smooth_sf %>% dplyr::filter(arm == a) %>% dplyr::select(value)
    rast <- make_raster_map(one, proj_crs, global_crs, "value")
    as.data.frame(rast, xy = TRUE, na.rm = FALSE) %>% mutate(arm = a)
  }
)

resid_lim <- max(abs(resid_raster_df$value), na.rm = TRUE)

# How much structure is there? SD of each smoothed surface (a flat surface ~ 0
# means no unmodelled spatial structure in that arm).
resid_smooth_sd <- resid_smooth %>%
  group_by(arm) %>%
  summarise(smooth_sd = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

resid_smooth_sd %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = paste(
    "SD of the arm-stratified smoothed Pearson-residual surface.",
    "Values near zero indicate no unmodelled spatial structure in that arm."))

resid_smooths <- base_map +
  geom_raster(data = resid_raster_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = value), na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_sf(data = niger_adm2_sub, fill = NA, color = "grey20", size = 0.15) +
  facet_wrap(~ arm, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = muted("#4B0055"), mid = "white", high = muted("#007D34"),
    midpoint = 0, limits = c(-resid_lim, resid_lim), na.value = NA,
    guide = guide_colorbar(title = "Smoothed Pearson residual (M1)",
                           title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5,
                           barheight = unit(10, "pt"), barwidth = unit(200, "pt")))

resid_smooths

ggsave(
  filename = here("results", "figs", "linearity-residual-smooths.png"),
  plot = resid_smooths, width = 8, height = 4.6, units = "in", dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

All scalars, tables, and derived surfaces this script produces, bundled for
downstream reference (e.g. the Methods/Discussion numbers and the supplement).

```{r save results object}

linearity_check <- list(
  # 4.2 surface agreement
  surface_cor_matrix = surface_cor_matrix,
  # 4.3 named scalars
  sd_delta          = sd_delta,          # SD of log RR from the M4 deviation field
  pct_rr_spread     = pct_rr_spread,     # ~ +/-% multiplicative spread in RR
  range_delta_km    = range_delta_km,    # deviation-field Matern range (interpretation)
  # 4.4 model comparison
  model_comparison  = model_comparison,
  lrt_m3_vs_m1      = lrt_m3,
  lrt_m4_vs_m1      = tibble(chi2_LR = chi2_m4, df = 1, p_value_mixture = p_m4_mixture),
  # 5.1 baseline vs RR
  baseline_rr_fit   = baseline_rr_fit,
  # 6 residual smooths
  resid_smooth_sd   = resid_smooth_sd
)

saveRDS(linearity_check, here("data", "linearity_check_results.rds"))
```

# Interpretation ----

Read together, these results are the anticipated **null**, framed as a bounded
magnitude rather than an absence of evidence:

- The four RR surfaces (4.1) are visually interchangeable and their predicted
  log RR correlates highly across every model pair (4.2).
- The plane (M1) has the lowest marginal AIC; M2–M4 are each several AIC units
  worse (4.4). The nested M3-vs-M1 test for curvature and diagonal structure is
  non-significant (4.4), and the M4 boundary test on the deviation variance is
  non-significant even before the conservative mixture correction.
- The M4 deviation field (4.3) contributes only short-range, village-level
  scatter (Matern range shorter than the village spacing), not a smooth spatial
  gradient the plane misses.
- Baseline mortality does **not** explain the ATE heterogeneity (5.1–5.2): the
  north–south baseline gradient and the east–west RR gradient are oblique, so
  the RR surface is its own signal, not a reflection of where mortality is high.

Bottom line: **consistent with the linear specification being adequate at the
resolution these data support.** M1 remains the primary model.
```
